metadata.description: A Unique name used for the Virtual Machine domain and also for generating resource names. Defaults to a value prefixed with "aiovm-".
Type of authentication to use on the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
SSH key or password for the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
The size of the VM, at least 16GB RAM is required

Initial MOTD - path: /etc/motd owner: root:root permissions: '0644' content: | +------------------------------------------------------------+ | Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Provisioning | +------------------------------------------------------------+ | Status: Starting Up... | | Action: Running cloud-init setup script | | | | To monitor progress in real-time (from another terminal): | | $ watch -n 1 -t cat /etc/motd | | | | Please wait for configuration to complete. | +------------------------------------------------------------+ # 2. The main provisioning script - path: /root/provision_ops_vm.sh owner: root:root permissions: '0700' # rwx------ (executable for root) content: | #!/bin/bash # Ensure script runs under bash and handle errors robustly # Exit on error (-e), error on undefined variable (-u), error on pipeline failure (-o pipefail) set -euo pipefail # --- Configuration --- TOTAL_STEPS=8 MOTD_WIDTH=62 # Total width including borders # --- Helper Function: update_motd --- # (Function definition remains the same as previous correct version) update_motd() { local step_num="$1" local status_msg="2" shift 2 \# Remove the first two arguments, remaining are detail lines \# Ensure details is treated as an array even if empty local details\=\("@") local text_width=$((MOTD_WIDTH - 4)) # Width available for text inside '* ... *' # Header printf '+%.0s' $(seq 1 $MOTD_WIDTH) > /etc/motd echo >> /etc/motd # Title/Step Info local step_info if [[ "$step_num" == "ERROR" || "$step_num" == "SUCCESS" ]]; then step_info="$status_msg" else step_info="Step $step_num of $TOTAL_STEPS: $status_msg" fi # Truncate step_info if it's too long if [ ${#step_info} -gt text\_width \]; then step\_info\="(echo "$step_info" | head -c \(\(text\_width \- 3\)\)\)\.\.\." fi local padding\=(( (text_width - \{\#step\_info\}\) / 2 \)\) local remainder\=(( (text_width - ${#step_info}) % 2 )) printf '| %*s%s%*s |\n' $padding "" "$step_info" $((padding + remainder)) "" >> /etc/motd # Separator (optional, if details exist) if [ ${#details[@]} -gt 0 ]; then printf '|%.0s' $(seq 1 \(\(MOTD\_WIDTH\-2\)\)\) \>\> /etc/motd echo '\|' \>\> /etc/motd fi \# Detail Lines \# Loop gracefully handles empty details array for detail in "{details[@]}"; do # Truncate long details to fit local truncated_detail="$detail" if [ ${#truncated_detail} -gt text\_width \]; then truncated\_detail\="(echo "$truncated_detail" | head -c \(\(text\_width \- 3\)\)\)\.\.\." fi local detail\_padding\=(( (text_width - \{\#truncated\_detail\}\) / 2 \)\) local detail\_remainder\=(( (text_width - ${#truncated_detail}) % 2 )) printf '| %*s%s%*s |\n' $detail_padding "" "$truncated_detail" $((detail_padding + detail_remainder)) "" >> /etc/motd done # Empty line for spacing before footer if details were printed if [ ${#details[@]} -gt 0 ]; then printf '|%*s|\n' $((MOTD_WIDTH-2)) "" >> /etc/motd fi # Footer printf '+%.0s' $(seq 1 MOTD\_WIDTH\) \>\> /etc/motd echo \>\> /etc/motd \} \# \-\-\- Error Handling Function \-\-\- handle\_error\(\) \{ local exit\_code\=? # BASH_LINENO is an array. [0] is the line number where the error occurred. local line_no=\{BASH\_LINENO\[0\]\:\-unknown\} \# BASH\_COMMAND contains the command that failed\. local command\="{BASH_COMMAND:-unknown}" # CORRECTED: Escape double quotes in the command before passing to update_motd local safe_command_hint=$(echo "command" \| sed 's/"/\\\\"/g'\) \# Further sanitize for control characters just in case safe\_command\_hint\=(echo "$safe_command_hint" | tr -dc '[:print:]') # Update MOTD with error details using the helper function update_motd "ERROR" "PROVISIONING FAILED!" \ "Script: /root/provision_ops_vm.sh" \ "Error on or near line: ${line_no}" \ "Exit Code: ${exit_code}" \ "Failed Command Hint: ${safe_command_hint}" \ # Use sanitized version "Check cloud-init logs:" \ "/var/log/cloud-init.log" \ "/var/log/cloud-init-output.log" # Exit with the original error code exit exit\_code \} \# \-\-\- Trap ERR signal \-\-\- \# This will now work correctly as the script file is executed by bash trap handle\_error ERR \# \-\-\- Start Provisioning Steps \-\-\- update\_motd "\.\.\." "Initializing Variables & Environment" \# Set environment variables used in later steps\. \# Make sure these are exported if needed by sub\-processes like az commands export MYUSER\=(id -un 1000) export MYHOME=$(eval echo ~MYUSER\) export MYWORK\="/workspaces" export LOCATION\="{LOCATION:-{{{location}}}" export RESOURCE_GROUP="\{RESOURCE\_GROUP\:\-\{\{\{resource\_group\}\}\}\}" export RESOURCE\_NAME\="{RESOURCE_NAME:-{{{resource_name}}}}" # Validate required variables are set if [[ "$LOCATION" == "{{{location}}}" || "$RESOURCE_GROUP" == "{{{resource_group}}}" || "RESOURCE\_NAME" \=\= "\{\{\{resource\_name\}\}\}" \]\]; then update\_motd "ERROR" "Missing Required Variables\!" \\ "LOCATION, RESOURCE\_GROUP, or RESOURCE\_NAME was not provided\." \\ "Check cloud\-init user\-data\." exit 1 fi \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- \# Step 1 of 8\: Install prerequisites\. \# \(Rest of the steps remain the same as the previous correct version\) \# \.\.\. \(Ensure all steps 1\-8 are present here as before\) \.\.\. \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- update\_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Checking package tools\.\.\." SYSTEM\_NAME\=(uname -r) if ! command -v k3d &> /dev/null; then update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Downloading & Installing k3d..." wget -q -O - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3d-io/k3d/main/install.sh | bash else update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "k3d already installed." fi if ! command -v helm &> /dev/null; then update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Downloading & Installing Helm..." # Use curl -fsSL for better error checking in pipelines curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash else update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Helm already installed." fi if ! command -v step &> /dev/null; then update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Downloading & Installing Step CLI..." STEP_VERSION="0.28.0" STEP_DEB="step-cli_${STEP_VERSION}_amd64.deb" STEP_TMP_DEB=$(mktemp --suffix=.deb) wget -qO "STEP\_TMP\_DEB" "https\://github\.com/smallstep/cli/releases/download/v{STEP_VERSION}/${STEP_DEB}" dpkg -i "$STEP_TMP_DEB" rm "$STEP_TMP_DEB" else update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Step CLI already installed." fi # Check Azure CLI (already installed via packages, but confirm `az` command) update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Verifying Azure CLI..." if ! command -v az &> /dev/null; then update_motd "ERROR" "Azure CLI Installation Failed!" "az command not found after package install." exit 1 fi update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Installing AKS CLI components..." # Run this even if az is present, might need updates/specific versions az aks install-cli --kubelogin-version 0.1.3 --aks-preview-cli-version 0.6.5 || echo "Warning: aks install-cli command finished with non-zero exit code." update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Adding/Updating Azure CLI extensions..." # Allow extension add to fail sometimes, just print warning az extension add --upgrade --name azure-iot-ops &> /dev/null || echo "Warning: Failed to add or upgrade 'azure-iot-ops' extension." az extension add --upgrade --name connectedk8s &> /dev/null || echo "Warning: Failed to add or upgrade 'connectedk8s' extension." if ! command -v k9s &> /dev/null; then update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Downloading & Installing k9s..." # Getting latest URL robustly K9S_DEB_URL=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/derailed/k9s/releases/latest | grep 'browser_download_url.*linux_amd64.deb' | head -n 1 | cut -d '"' -f 4) if [[ -n "K9S\_DEB\_URL" \]\]; then \# Create temporary file securely K9S\_TMP\_DEB\=(mktemp --suffix=.deb) wget -qO "$K9S_TMP_DEB" "$K9S_DEB_URL" dpkg -i "$K9S_TMP_DEB" rm "$K9S_TMP_DEB" # Clean up downloaded file else update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "Warning: Could not determine k9s latest deb URL. Skipping." fi else update_motd "1" "Installing prerequisites" "k9s already installed." fi # ------------------------- # Step 2 of 8: Create k3d cluster. # ------------------------- update_motd "2" "Creating k3d cluster" "Checking existing k3d cluster..." # If cluster exists and is running, maybe skip? For simplicity, we recreate. if k3d cluster list | grep -q '^k3s-default'; then update_motd "2" "Creating k3d cluster" "Deleting existing k3s-default cluster..." k3d cluster delete k3s-default || true # Allow failure if deletion has issues but continue fi update_motd "2" "Creating k3d cluster" "Creating new cluster 'k3s-default'..." "This may take a few minutes." k3d cluster create k3s-default \ -p '1883:1883@loadbalancer' \ -p '8883:8883@loadbalancer' \ -p '8884:8884@loadbalancer' \ --registry-create k3d-registry.localhost:127.0.0.1:5000 \ --wait update_motd "2" "Creating k3d cluster" "Configuring kubectl context..." mkdir -p "$MYHOME/.kube" # Let k3d merge into the default config directly k3d kubeconfig merge k3s-default --kubeconfig-merge-default # Ensure user owns their config chown "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.kube" chown "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.kube/config" chmod 600 "$MYHOME/.kube/config" # Set context for root user running the script and the target user kubectl config use-context k3d-k3s-default kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=azure-iot-operations # Ensure user context is also set (run as the user) sudo -u "$MYUSER" KUBECONFIG="$MYHOME/.kube/config" kubectl config use-context k3d-k3s-default sudo -u "$MYUSER" KUBECONFIG="$MYHOME/.kube/config" kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=azure-iot-operations # ------------------------- # Step 3 of 8: Arc-enable the Kubernetes cluster. # ------------------------- update_motd "3" "Azure Arc Connection" "Logging into Azure (Managed Identity)..." az login --identity --output none # Suppress login output update_motd "3" "Azure Arc Connection" "Connecting cluster to Arc..." "Resource: $RESOURCE_NAME" "RG: $RESOURCE_GROUP" "Location: $LOCATION" # Using default kubeconfig which root now uses az connectedk8s connect --name "$RESOURCE_NAME" --location "$LOCATION" --resource-group "RESOURCE\_GROUP" \-\-correlation\-id "" \-\-output none \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- \# Step 4 of 8\: Create Storage Account\. \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- \# Generate a unique name for the storage account \# Max 24 chars, lowercase alphanumeric UNIQUE\_SUFFIX\=(echo "RESOURCE\_NAME" \| sha256sum \| head \-c 10\) \# Use hash for uniqueness STORAGE\_ACCOUNT\="st(echo "$RESOURCE_NAME" | tr -cd '[:alnum:]' | head -c 10)UNIQUE\_SUFFIX" STORAGE\_ACCOUNT\=(echo "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | head -c 24) update_motd "4" "Azure Storage Account" "Checking for account: $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" # Check existence using 'az storage account show' and check exit code if az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --output none &> /dev/null; then update_motd "4" "Azure Storage Account" "Account $STORAGE_ACCOUNT already exists." else update_motd "4" "Azure Storage Account" "Creating account: $STORAGE_ACCOUNT..." "RG: $RESOURCE_GROUP" "Location: $LOCATION" az storage account create --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --location "$LOCATION" --resource-group "RESOURCE\_GROUP" \-\-enable\-hierarchical\-namespace true \-\-sku Standard\_RAGRS \-\-kind StorageV2 \-\-output none fi update\_motd "4" "Azure Storage Account" "Retrieving Resource ID\.\.\." SA\_RESOURCE\_ID\=(az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv) if [[ -z "$SA_RESOURCE_ID" ]]; then update_motd "ERROR" "Failed to get Storage Account ID!" "Account: STORAGE\_ACCOUNT" exit 1 fi export SA\_RESOURCE\_ID \# Export for subsequent steps if needed directly \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- \# Step 5 of 8\: Create Schema Registry\. \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- \# Generate unique names SR\_SUFFIX\_HASH\=(echo "RESOURCE\_NAME" \| sha256sum \| head \-c 10\) SCHEMA\_REGISTRY\="sr(echo "$RESOURCE_NAME" | tr -cd '[:alnum:]' | head -c 10)SR\_SUFFIX\_HASH" SCHEMA\_REGISTRY\=(echo "SCHEMA\_REGISTRY" \| tr '\[\:upper\:\]' '\[\:lower\:\]' \| head \-c 24\) SCHEMA\_REGISTRY\_NAMESPACE\="srn(echo "$RESOURCE_NAME" | tr -cd '[:alnum:]' | head -c 10)SR\_SUFFIX\_HASH" SCHEMA\_REGISTRY\_NAMESPACE\=(echo "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | head -c 24) update_motd "5" "Azure Schema Registry" "Checking for registry: $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" if az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --output none &> /dev/null; then update_motd "5" "Azure Schema Registry" "Registry $SCHEMA_REGISTRY already exists." else update_motd "5" "Azure Schema Registry" "Creating registry: $SCHEMA_REGISTRY..." "Namespace: $SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE" "RG: $RESOURCE_GROUP" az iot ops schema registry create --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --registry-namespace "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE" --sa-resource-id "$SA_RESOURCE_ID" --output none fi # ------------------------- # Step 6 of 8: Initialize IoT Operations. # ------------------------- update_motd "6" "Azure IoT Operations Init" "Checking initialization status..." "Cluster: $RESOURCE_NAME" # Check if key CRDs or namespace resources exist if ! kubectl get ns azure-iot-operations &> /dev/null || ! kubectl get deployment mq-operator -n azure-iot-operations &> /dev/null; then update_motd "6" "Azure IoT Operations Init" "Running az iot ops init..." "Cluster: $RESOURCE_NAME" "RG: $RESOURCE_GROUP" "(Using --no-tls for k3d)" # Assuming --no-tls for k3d simplicity, adjust if using KeyVault az iot ops init --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --no-tls --no-progress else update_motd "6" "Azure IoT Operations Init" "Already initialized." "Cluster: RESOURCE\_NAME" fi \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- \# Step 7 of 8\: Create IoT Ops Instance\. \# \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- update\_motd "7" "Azure IoT Ops Instance" "Retrieving Schema Registry ID\.\.\." SR\_RESOURCE\_ID\=(az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv) if [[ -z "$SR_RESOURCE_ID" ]]; then update_motd "ERROR" "Failed to get Schema Registry ID!" "Registry: SCHEMA\_REGISTRY" exit 1 fi INSTANCE\_NAME\="{RESOURCE_NAME}-instance" update_motd "7" "Azure IoT Ops Instance" "Checking for instance: $INSTANCE_NAME" # Check if the Broker resource exists as an indicator if ! kubectl get broker "$INSTANCE_NAME" -n azure-iot-operations &> /dev/null; then update_motd "7" "Azure IoT Ops Instance" "Creating instance: $INSTANCE_NAME..." "Cluster: $RESOURCE_NAME" "RG: $RESOURCE_GROUP" "(Low profile, RF=1)" az iot ops instance create \ --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" \ --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \ --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" \ --sr-resource-id "$SR_RESOURCE_ID" \ --broker-frontend-replicas 1 \ --broker-frontend-workers 1 \ --broker-backend-part 1 \ --broker-backend-workers 1 \ --broker-backend-rf 1 \ --broker-mem-profile Low \ --no-progress \ --output none else update_motd "7" "Azure IoT Ops Instance" "Instance $INSTANCE_NAME already exists." fi # ------------------------- # Step 8 of 8: Configure kube config and Finalize. # ------------------------- update_motd "8" "Finalizing Setup" "Ensuring kubeconfig permissions..." "User: $MYUSER" # Re-apply ownership/permissions just in case chown "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.kube/config" chmod 600 "$MYHOME/.kube/config" update_motd "8" "Finalizing Setup" "Setting workspace ownership..." "Path: $MYWORK" mkdir -p "$MYWORK" chown -R "$MYUSER":"$MYUSER" "$MYWORK" # ------------------------- # Final Success Message # ------------------------- # Disable the error trap cleanly before final MOTD update trap - ERR update_motd "SUCCESS" "PROVISIONING COMPLETE!" \ "System is ready." \ "Kubeconfig set for user '$MYUSER'" \ "Try: kubectl get pods -A" \ "Try: k9s" echo "Script /root/provision_ops_vm.sh finished successfully." # runcmd executes the script written above by the write_files module runcmd: - /root/provision_ops_vm.sh
